entry.dc:title: Conversion from Trucks to Conveyor Belts in Open Pit Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Streck W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: Conversion from trucks to conveyor belts is a possibility to reduce production costs. In two projects, coal is conventionally loaded for truck transportation to transfer points at the stopes where it is belt-conveyed to dumps. Caterpillar-mounted crushers with prescreening units and mobile conveyor belts follow extraction from stope to stope. The conveyor belts are suitable for coarse and abrasive material.

entry.dc:title: SANDWICH BELT HIGH ANGLE CONVEYORS - APPLICATIONS IN OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Dos Santos J.
entry.dc:description: High angle conveyor (HAC) systems in open pit mining offer many advantages over the traditional, truck only, haulage systems. The present paper introduces the Continental Conveyor sandwich belt HAC as the vital link to optimization of in-pit conveying systems. Discussion continues with the HAC systems to suit the various open pit mining operations and the corresponding characteristics of the system components, particularly the high angle conveyor.

entry.dc:title: CHALLENGING DREDGE MINING PROJECT UNDERWAY IN THOMPSON, CANADA.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The purpose of this project is to expose an orebody for Inco's open pit mining scheduled to go into production in early 1986. Thompson Open Pit is Inco Limited's largest mining development project currently underway at any of its worldwide locations. The project involves mining a portion of the Thompson orebody from the surface at a location near the company's processing complex at Thompson.

entry.dc:title: HYDROLOGIC SITE SELECTION FOR MINING OF DEEP BASIN LIGNITE IN TEXAS.
entry.dc:creator: Charbeneau R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Technical Report University of Texas at Austin Center for Research in Water Resources
entry.dc:description: Texas lignite will be the fuel preferred by many of the state's utilities and industries. Near surface lignite reserves are adequate to meet the needs of the early decades of the 21st century. Meeting the demands of the decades beyond will require the recovery of deep basin lignite or a transition to alternative energy fuels. The subject of this research is the hydrological and geomechanical feasibility and impact of open pit mining and underground coal gasification for recovery of deep basin Texas lignite. Of major concern are the quantities and uses of water from site dewatering and depressurizing operations, the stability of open pit mine slopes and how it is influenced by water, and the regional hydrologic impacts of lignite mining. Refs.

entry.dc:title: WEST GERMAN OPEN PIT MINING TECHNOLOGY FOR AUSTRALIAN HARD COAL MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The first giant bucket wheel excavator system for the Bowen Basin coalfields in Queensland (Australia) has been commissioned at the Goonyella mine owned by Central Queensland Coal Associates. The excavator has a theoretical output of 5200m**3/h (loose) and a guaranteed output of 1500m**3/h (bank). The bucket wheel has a diameter of 12. 25m with ten buckets plus ten pre-cutters, each bucket having a nominal capacity of 1. 8m**3.

entry.dc:title: USE OF AIRCRAFT IMAGERY IN EVALUATING GROUND STABILITY AT OPEN PIT URANIUM MINES IN GAS HILLS, WYOMING.
entry.dc:creator: Stahl R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Informational Report U S Department of Labor Mine Safety and Health Administration
entry.dc:description: This report presents an approach used by Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) and mine operators to evaluate ground stability in open pit mining operations in the Gas Hills, Wyoming. The approach uses aircraft imagery to identify geology features, such as fractures and faults, that can affect ground stability in surface mines. Operators in the Gas Hills are using this technology as a mine planning and design to avoid or to minimize the effects of fractures and faults on ground stability. This remote sensing tool is appealing because it is inexpensive, accurate and one that permits rapid evaluation of a mining area on a local and regional scale.

entry.dc:title: OPTIMIZATION OF PRODUCTIVITY OF MINING EQUIPMENT SYSTEMS.
entry.dc:creator: Dickerson A.W.
entry.dc:description: The operation of equipment in a mine produces a complex system which requires monitoring, simulation, analysis, and reconciliation to insure optimum production. The work described in the paper represents the initial step in an overall program to enable optimization of production and equipment usage. Two areas of investigation are covered in some detail. The first concerns large haul trucks which accomplish much of the movement of minerals and wastes in many open pit mining operations. The monitoring of trucks in normal operation is described along with some of the results of such work. The second concerns draglines which are similarly important in moving overburden in many coal mines. A program of computer simulation of draglines is described.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPMENT TRENDS IN THE CONSTRUCTION OF SPREADERS FOR OPENCAST MINE DUMPS: PART 1. SPREADERS IN AROUND-THE-PIT PRE-STRIPPING SYSTEMS.
entry.dc:creator: Bartsch D.
entry.dc:description: A survey of the current methods in excavation of overburden in open pit mining operations is given. The article highlights the output which may be achieved by one machine or system, depending upon specific conditions such as geologic or climatic constraints.

entry.dc:title: QUINTETTE OPERATION REQUIRES CAREFUL EQUIPMENT SELECTION.
entry.dc:creator: Pelley M.H.
entry.dc:description: Over the next twenty years, the Quintette project will involve the development of the McConkey, Frame, Shikano and Babcock open pit mining areas. To facilitate the selection and sizing of the mining equipment, all waste and coal types were identified and quantified based on materials handling requirements.

entry.dc:title: Tar Sand Mining in Canada - a Technological Challenge.
entry.dc:creator: Boehm F.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: The deposits consist of 180 multiplied by 10**9 m**3 bitumen in situ and cover an area of 70,000 km**2. Only 7% are classified for open pit mining. The climate with temperatures of minus 45 degree C during the winter and plus 35 degree C in summer, wind, ice and snow are a challenge for men and machine. The abrasiveness and oily characteristics of the sand cause material problems which could only be overcome through research and development programs. Two companies are presently mining in open pits. Both operators have to move high volumes of sand, bitumen and water. The mining methods are different - in one case using bucket wheel excavaters and in the other a combination of dragline and bucket wheel reclaimers. Both methods are described.

entry.dc:title: ENERGY CONSUMPTION IN OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Nilsson D.
entry.dc:description: This article evaluates energy consumption in overburden stripping using draglines, shovels and trucks, and scrapers in a hypothetical open pit coal mine. The dragline gives the lowest cost, at 0. 43 per ton. However, no account has been taken of capital costs, wages, etc.

entry.dc:title: COMBINED GEOTECHNICAL AND HYDROLOGIC STUDIES OF THE YANKEE DOODLE TAILINGS DAM.
entry.dc:creator: Poindexter D.
entry.dc:description: The Yankee Doodle tailings dam is a massive rockfill embankment adjacent to the Berkeley Pit mine, which is one of the largest open pit mining operations in North America. The mine, tailings retention pond, processing plant, water supply system, and all appurtenant facilities necessary to produce copper concentrate at the Butte, Montana site are operated by the Anaconda Copper Company. The original structure was designed 20 years ago, and the purposes of this study were to determine present conditions within the dam, to evaluate the capacity of the hydrologic system, to investigate the seismicity of the area and determine the resistance of the dam to earthquake loadings, and to study the effects of operational techniques including continuous construction and leaching operations near to, and on, the dam. Monitoring and observation of project variables are recommended concurrent with continuing enlargement of the dam to the final design height.

entry.dc:title: Increase of Holding and Carrying Capacities of Cars for Open Pit Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Sheshko E.
entry.dc:description: The design of dump cars with the holding capacity of up to 200-250 m**3 and the carrying capacity of up to 400-500t is considered. Hopper-type cars on two-axle paired bogies, capable of withstanding loads of up to 350 kn per axle, traveling on a 4-rail track having a total width of 5620 mm, are proposed for the Ekabastuz open pit mines.

entry.dc:title: LARGE ROCK CONVEYING SYSTEMS AND THEIR APPLICATION IN OPEN-PIT MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Martin T.W.
entry.dc:description: Two large rock conveyor concepts have been developed and a test facility investigation designed and fabricated. The USBM will test these concepts along with loading and transfer points for handling material up to 1. 5 m (4. 9 ft) in size. An evaluation of open pit mining systems using large rock conveyors documents cost savings compared to truck haulage.

entry.dc:title: NEW DEVELOPMENTS IN VERTICAL CONVEYING WITH SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON THE TRANSSHIPMENT OF BULK MATERIALS.
entry.dc:creator: Paelke J.
entry.dc:description: A new vertical conveying method based on the FLEXOWELL-technology is introduced, which lends itself to vertical and inclined bulk solids conveying in deep shafts, in open pit mining, in processing plants and blast furnace charging, in filling silos and dumps, and especially for unloading of ships.

entry.dc:title: Investigation of Humidity and Friability of Coals from New Kuzbas Deposits.
entry.dc:creator: Novitskii N.
entry.dc:description: Data on moisture content and friability of coals from newly discovered coal fields in the Kuzbas (Talda, Urop, Karakan, Novokazanskoye, etc. ) are presented. These fields will have to be developed in the future by the open pit mining method. Each mine will have up to 30 Mt capacity. Many coals have high moisture content and poor friability.

entry.dc:title: TRANSPORT WITH LARGE CONVEYORS IN SURFACE MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Lubrich W.
entry.dc:description: An attempt is made to differentiate between the criteria usually required for the design of conveyor systems under ordinary operating conditions and those with which open-pit planners will be increasingly concerned in the future. Based on the well-known relationship between lifting power requirements, the calculation of the power requirement for conveyor equipment is shown by calculating the local belt pull. Finally, attention is drawn to the dynamic behavior of the transport of single large lumps and the possibility of assessing the respective forces is indicated, in view of the growing importance of handling these lumps in hard rock and also in soft rock open pit mining.

entry.dc:title: CONTINUOUS CONVEYING IN OPEN PIT MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Glanz W.
entry.dc:description: Various open pit mining systems with hard rock and unconsolidated overburden are analyzed and the main differences between discontinuous, semi-continuous and fully continuous mining and transportation methods are outlined. It is demonstrated that future open pit mining systems will tend to use continuous or semi-continuous haulage and mining operations in which detailed, long-term economic and technical planning and evaluation with the help of computer programs will play a major role.

entry.dc:title: A New Concept for Wheel Loaders in Open Pit Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Gradenegger H.
entry.dc:description: A new type of wheel loader is described which is distinguished by a favorable payload-to-weight ratio, low fuel consumption, high stability and low turning radius (ensuring good loading and transport performance), good driving characteristics, and driving comfort. These qualities are achieved by designing the wheel loader as a rigid frame, which also ensures low-cost construction.

entry.dc:title: A study of radiation parameters in an open PIT mine
entry.dc:creator: Leach V.A.
entry.dc:description: Radiation parameters associated with the open pit mining of a small (10,000 tonnes), but high grade (2) uranium deposit at Nabarlek, N.T., have been investigated in detail. External radiation levels, radon emanation rates and radon daughter levels were measured systematically during the development of the mine, and are correlated with ore grade, properties of the host rock and atmospheric conditions. Significant radon daughter concentrations were observed only under stable atmospheric conditions, usually during the night and were invariably associated with thermal inversions. The mean cumulative exposure to radon daughters was estimated from the measured levels to be 0.065 Working Level Months for employees working in the pit for the entire four and a half months of mining. The mean cumulative external gamma ray exposure for the same employee group was measured using thermoluminescent dosimeters to be 2.3 mSv (230 mrem). For most other employees, however, exposures were much lower. Data on long lived radionuclides in dust and on particle size distribution are also presented. © 1982 Health Physics Society Pergamon Press Ltd.

entry.dc:title: Recovery of Metal Values from Low Grade Copper Sulfide Ores
entry.dc:creator: Wadsworth M.E.
entry.dc:description: In the United States approximately 12 percent of the new copper produced comes from dump leaching of low grade waste rock from open pit mining. While this amount of copper is significant it is unusual, even for massive dumps, for steady-state recovery rates to exceed 20 percent. Basic physical and chemical features important in leaching typical copper porphyry waste rock have been determined in laboratory studies in tests involving up to several tons of waste rock. The important findings of such tests including chemistry of extraction, laboratory modeling, energy implications, and recovery from dilute streams are presented. Special emphasis is given to important rate limiting features of waste rock leaching including the role of autotrophic bacteria in the oxidation sequence. Difficulties in scale up from the laboratory to practice are discussed. Copyright © 1981,, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Tailings disposal concepts in oil sands open pit mining.
entry.dc:creator: Mittal H.
entry.dc:description: This paper presents a state-of-the-art description of the procedures currently used which have evolved in this industry for the design and operation of these tailings disposal schemes. Some of the innovative techniques presently being considered for further design optimizations in terms of cost effectiveness, environmental concerns and resource conservation aspects are also discussed. (from paper)

entry.dc:title: Practical experience with centrifugal pumps in mine dewatering application.
entry.dc:creator: Kosyna G.
entry.prism:issueIdentifier: (Braunschweig, Fed. Rep. Germany: Oct. 14-16, 1981), Dusseldorf, Fed. Rep. Germany, VDI-Verlag GmbH,
entry.dc:description: This paper shows typical installations of dewatering pumps in underground and open pit mining and gives a brief introduction to mine dewatering problems. Environmental conditions as well as the urgency of cost reduction of mine dewatering systems impose design objectives on pumps for mine dewatering. (A)

entry.dc:title: LODEVE - A NEW URANIUM MINE IN FRANCE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: A mine and concentrator recently constructed by Compagnie generale des matieres nucleaires (Cogema) is situated near Lodeve in Herault, where a series of uranium bearing beds was discovered in 1957. Open pit mining started in 1978. An underground mine has been developed and a concentrator will be ready to start up early in 1981.

entry.dc:title: Raw material extraction in open pit mining considerations of environmental compatibility
entry.dc:creator: Thiede H.
